title: Brussels Anti-Slavery Conference 1889–90
summary: The English Wikipedia article "Brussels Anti-Slavery Conference 1889–90", at revision 1381620987, opens: "The Brussels Anti-Slavery Conference of 1889–1890 was held from 18 November 1889 to 2 July 1890 in Brussels and concluded with the adoption of the Brussels Conference Act of 1890 on the prohibition of slave trade and slavery in Africa. The convention favoured colonial policies, justified by the anti-slavery argument. The event and its origins were shaped primarily by a narrow national interest. Governments paid lip service to humanitarian goals in order to legitimize their imperial aims." That is the article's account and not yet this atlas's; nobody has read this record, and review.html is where somebody does. Wikidata item Q16889931, imported by tools/import/wikidata.mjs. The item's own description reads "Conference leading to prohibition of slavery in Africa". Everything here is copied from the item's own fields and nothing in it is this atlas's account of the thing: that is still to be written, and review.html is where somebody writes it.
